scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: I think the answer is 1, which means YTA (You're The Asshole). Your son is 19, which means he's an adult and capable of making his own decisions. By showing up unannounced, you may have made him feel like you're not trusting him to take care of himself or that you're trying to exert control over his life. Additionally, your son has explicitly told you that he needs space and that you should give it to him when he needs it. Ignoring his request and showing up anyway can be seen as dismissive of his feelings and needs. It's understandable that you're concerned about your son's well-being, especially given the state of his apartment. However, addressing these concerns in a respectful and considerate manner would be more effective than showing up unannounced. You could have tried calling or texting him to express your concerns and ask if everything is okay, rather than taking matters into your own hands. It's also worth considering that your son may be going through a period of adjustment and exploration as a young adult, and that his behavior may not be about ignoring you, but about establishing his own independence and identity. Giving him space and respecting his boundaries can help you build a stronger and more trusting relationship with him in the long run.
